tasks.title: A local dashboard build never breaks the running Mac dashboard
tasks.notes: Options: server re-reads `runtime-assets.js` when react-dist changes, or build writes to a staging dir and swaps atomically, then signals the server.

prep.what: Make the Vite build output atomic so a running Mac dashboard is never served a half-updated JS bundle.
prep.understand: The Mac server reads from the build output dir. A mid-flight build overwrites files the server is actively serving, causing 404s or broken state. Atomic swap (write to staging, rename) prevents this entirely.
approach: Find current build output path (likely `react-dist/`) and how the server reads `runtime-assets.js` on startup.
Implement atomic swap: build to a staging dir (e.g. `react-dist-next/`), then `fs.rename()` over `react-dist/` and send SIGUSR1 to the server to reload.
Alternative if rename is complex: add a file-watcher on `runtime-assets.js` so the server re-reads it on change.
Test: trigger `npm run build` while the dashboard is open in a browser; confirm no broken state or downtime.
resources: Mac dashboard server startup / signal handler

tasks.title: Dismissed and legacy-closed requests stop showing clients a live status
tasks.notes: V1 stabilization K2. The DB CHECK already prevents silent revival. Real defect: raw 400 on client reply needs to become 404. 6 dismissed/Done requests are live in the system.

prep.what: Stop dismissed and legacy-closed client requests from showing a live status or leaking a raw 400 when a client tries to reply to them.
prep.understand: K2 of V1 stabilization. The DB CHECK already blocks silent revival, so the transactional safety is there. The surface bug: clients see a raw 400 (not 404) on reply, and their list view still shows these requests as active. 6 dismissed/Done requests are currently live.
approach: Read K2 in `docs/current/v1-stabilization-audit-2026-09-28.md` for the exact endpoints and fix spec.
Find the client-reply endpoint: change the 400 from the CHECK violation to a clean 404 with a safe message ('Request not found').
Update the client-facing request list query to filter out `dismissed` and `legacy-closed` statuses.
Smoke-test with one of the 6 known affected requests: reply should return 404; request should not appear in the client list.
resources: 6 known dismissed/Done request IDs (in the audit doc or DB)

tasks.title: Build on-device scan diagnostics and session export
tasks.phase: Scanner Evidence — Make Tracking Failures Observable
tasks.notes: Record tracking state, plane/depth availability, camera pose, locked-corner samples, rejection reasons, and timing without collecting camera imagery by default.

prep.what: Build a diagnostics module that records the scanner’s internal state every frame (no camera pixels) and lets you export the session log as JSON.
prep.understand: Phase 1 goal: make tracking failures observable before trying to fix them. ARCore’s `Frame.getTrackingState()`, `TrackingFailureReason`, depth availability, and corner lock events are the signals. A serializable per-session log lets you replay failure conditions on a desk.
approach: Design `DiagnosticsSession` data class: fields for `trackingState`, `trackingFailureReason`, `planeCount`, `depthAvailable`, `cornerLockEvents[]`, `rejectionReasons[]`, timestamps — no pixel buffers.
Hook into the ARCore `Session.update()` callback; sample state on change or ~2 fps (not every frame — stay cheap).
Add an export function: serialize to JSON, write to `Context.getExternalFilesDir(Environment.DIRECTORY_DOWNLOADS)`, share via `FileProvider` + `Intent.ACTION_SEND`.
Verify no camera imagery is ever stored: no `ImageReader`, no `AugmentedImage` pixel captures, no `Frame.acquireCameraImage()` calls in the new code.
resources: Existing scanner session / ARCore session code in the repo

tasks.title: Create the structured S25 room-scan test matrix
tasks.phase: Scanner Evidence — Make Tracking Failures Observable
tasks.notes: Define repeatable cases for small/large rooms, plain walls, textured walls, reflective floors, low light, clutter, openings, and temporary tracking loss.

prep.what: Write a repeatable test document for S25 room-scan scenarios — each row is a setup, expected ARCore behavior, and pass/fail threshold.
prep.understand: You can’t stabilize what you can’t measure. This matrix is your before/after baseline for every scanner change. S25 has specific IMU and camera characteristics; the `TrackingFailureReason` enum names the failure modes to cover. Pair each scenario with the diagnostics export from p1t0.
approach: List all scanner failure modes: plain walls, reflective floors, low light, clutter, small rooms (<3m), large rooms (>8m), doorways/openings, temporary tracking loss.
For each scenario: define physical setup, expected `TrackingState` progression, pass threshold (e.g. ‘locks 4 corners within 30s’), and which `TrackingFailureReason` to watch for.
Create `tests/scan-test-matrix.md` (or wherever test docs live) with a Markdown table per scenario group.
Link each scenario to the diagnostics export fields from p1t0 so you know exactly what to capture during the test run.
resources: Samsung S25 ARCore compatibility / IMU notes
Existing test docs in `/tests` if any
